key_insight: Bidding determines both advertising outcomes and access to price information, making media trading a joint control-and-learning problem under censored auction prices.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports bidding-system design that balances campaign performance, transaction margins, finite budgets, and price exploration.
method: Model bidding as continuous-time stochastic control with latent market prices.
Estimate prices using parallel exploratory subcampaigns with randomized, upper-bounded bids.
Compute policies via forward-equation calibration, HJB policy iteration and a physics-informed neural network, or observable-information entropy-regularized actor-critic learning.
evidence_signal: Synthetic experiments illustrate estimation and computation; under a stylized cross-sectional sampling model, the price estimator is consistent with mean-square error of order N⁻¹.
watch_item: Full-information benchmarks and estimated-price policies do not resolve the genuinely partially observed problem, and real-world validation is not reported in the abstract.
paper_title: Media Trading with Censored Auction Prices: A Stochastic Control and Reinforcement Learning Approach
